items.title: Signs of Oil Pump Failure: Warning Checklist
items.description: Identify whether you are experiencing early oil delivery warnings or progressed mechanical damage.

cards.title: Flickering Oil Light at Idle:
cards.text: Flickering Oil Light at Idle: Oil pressure warning light blinks when stationary at idle but extinguishes when revving above 1,500 RPM. Hydraulic Lifter Ticking: Tapping or clicking noises originating from the top of the cylinder head due to oil starvation at the camshafts. Low Oil Pressure Gauge: Analogue or digital dashboard oil pressure gauge registers below manufacturer operating threshold (under 1.5–2.0 bar warm).

cards.title: Solid Oil Pressure Warning Light:
cards.text: Solid Oil Pressure Warning Light: Red oil can symbol remains illuminated permanently at all engine speeds. Loud Deep Rhythmic Knocking: Rhythmic heavy thudding under load indicates big-end rod bearing clearance failure. Engine Squeal or Sudden Drag: Friction welding between bearing surfaces causes sudden engine drag, loss of RPM, and burning oil smell. Engine Seizure / No Crank: Starter motor clicks but cannot turn the crankshaft due to seized bottom-end journals.

items.title: Why Oil Pump Failure Causes Secondary Bearing Damage
items.description: Understanding the physics of hydrodynamic wedge lubrication and why failure occurs in seconds.

cards.title: hydrodynamic oil wedge
cards.text: The oil pump forces engine oil through microscopic clearances (0.025–0.050mm) between spinning crankshaft journals and shell bearings. As the crankshaft rotates, it creates a high-pressure hydrodynamic oil wedge that literally floats the multi-ton reciprocating loads without allowing any metal-to-metal contact.
cards.fullText: 🛡️ How Oil Pressure Protects Your Engine The oil pump forces engine oil through microscopic clearances (0.025–0.050mm) between spinning crankshaft journals and shell bearings. As the crankshaft rotates, it creates a high-pressure hydrodynamic oil wedge that literally floats the multi-ton reciprocating loads without allowing any metal-to-metal contact.

cards.title: 1. Oil Film Collapse:
cards.text: 1. Oil Film Collapse: Pressurised cushion drains away under explosive combustion load. 2. Metal-on-Metal Contact: Crankshaft journal grinds directly against bearing shell. 3. Instant Thermal Spike: Friction generates temperatures exceeding 600°C in seconds. 4. Babbit Melting: Soft bearing surface layer melts and strips away into oil passages. 5. Spun Bearing: Bearing shell locks to the rotating crank journal and spins in the rod housing. 6. Catastrophic Rod Snapping: Rod snaps under stress and punches through the cylinder block.

blocks.text: Crucial Mechanical Fact: This destructive sequence does not take hours—it takes minutes or seconds under engine load. That is why an illuminated red oil pressure light is classified as an absolute stop-driving emergency.

cards.title: Likely Root Cause
cards.text: Internal oil pump gear wear, partial pickup strainer sludge blockage, or sticking oil pressure relief valve. Pressure is intermittently low at low RPM.

cards.text: Stop driving immediately. Book a diagnostic pressure gauge inspection. If caught immediately before knocking begins, pump replacement alone will preserve the engine.

cards.text: Degraded oil forms heavy carbon sludge that clogs the pickup mesh. Change oil every 6k–10k miles using strict OEM specifications.

cards.title: What are the signs of oil pump failure? +
cards.text: Common symptoms include: low oil pressure warning light (especially flickering at warm idle), ticking or tapping noise from hydraulic valve lifters, analogue pressure gauge dropping below normal, deep knocking noises from connecting rod bearings, and sudden engine seizure.
cards.fullText: What are the signs of oil pump failure? + Common symptoms include: low oil pressure warning light (especially flickering at warm idle), ticking or tapping noise from hydraulic valve lifters, analogue pressure gauge dropping below normal, deep knocking noises from connecting rod bearings, and sudden engine seizure.

cards.title: Can I drive with low oil pressure? +
cards.text: No. If the red oil pressure warning light illuminates, you must stop driving immediately and switch off the engine. Driving for even 30 seconds with zero oil pressure will overheat and destroy the crankshaft bearings.
cards.fullText: Can I drive with low oil pressure? + No. If the red oil pressure warning light illuminates, you must stop driving immediately and switch off the engine. Driving for even 30 seconds with zero oil pressure will overheat and destroy the crankshaft bearings.

cards.title: What causes oil pump failure? +
cards.text: Primary causes include: worn internal pump gears from high mileage, rounded balance shaft hex drive shafts (VAG EA189), clogged pickup strainer mesh from oil sludge or timing belt rubber debris (Ford EcoBoost), failed oil pressure relief valves, and housing stress fractures (Land Rover 276DT).
cards.fullText: What causes oil pump failure? + Primary causes include: worn internal pump gears from high mileage, rounded balance shaft hex drive shafts (VAG EA189), clogged pickup strainer mesh from oil sludge or timing belt rubber debris (Ford EcoBoost), failed oil pressure relief valves, and housing stress fractures (Land Rover 276DT).
